sentences.text: Shri Vivek Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri Abhishek Tugnawat, learned Govt. Advocate for the respondent/State.
Heard.
The present petition is arising out of the order dated 22.10.2019 passed by the Collector, Ujjain in exercise of powers conferred upon National Security Act, 1980.
The facts of the case reveals that the petitioner is a trader and has stated that without granting any opportunity of hearing, the order has been passed under the NSA Act.
Contention of the petitioner is that on 31.10.2018, some complaint was made to the Collector, Ujjain and a raid was conducted at Ashwini Traders.

Allegedly, adulterated Mava (condensed milk product) was seized from the spot and a case was registered against the petitioner for offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC alongwith Sections 50, 51 and 58 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

In respect of the criminal case, the present petitioner has preferred an application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail and the bail was granted to him by learned single Judge vide order dated 22.10.2019 passed in MCRC No.43235/2019.
However, based upon the same order and one more case of the year 2016, the order was passed by the District Magistrate under Section 3(2) of the NSA Act, 1980.

The petitioner came up before this Court and has stated that the alleged adulterated Mava was sent to Referral Food Laboratory,
Mysore and a report was received on 31.10.2019 stating categorically that the sample confirms the standards laid down for Mava/Khoya under the provisions of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulation 2 WP-28578-2019 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulation 2 WP-28578-2019 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Meaning thereby, it was not at all adulterated.

It is true that earlier, a report was submitted by Food Analyst stating that the Mava is of sub-standard quality, however, the Lab which is under the control of Government of India, which is much advance Lab has given a finding of the fact in favour of the petitioner.

sentences.text: This Court, in order to ascertain the correctness of the document (Annexure P/9) Page 32, which is a report filed alongwith the writ petition given by the Referral Food Laboratory, Mysore has directed the Collector to submit an affidavit and the Collector has submitted an affidavit stating that the report is correct and it is in respect of the same sample, meaning thereby, the basis on which an order under the National Security Act was passed against the petitioner is no longer in existence.
In light of the affidavit submitted by the Collector, Ujjain, this Court is left with no other choice except to quash the order dated 22.10.2019.
Resultantly, the petition stands allowed and the order dated 22.10.2019 is hereby quashed.
Cc as per rules.
S.C.SHARMA) (SHAILENDRA SHUKLA)
